answers.answer: ADK-JS integrates with OpenTelemetry by initializing a tracer with the name 'gcp.vertex.agent' and the ADK version. Span creation occurs for agent invocations (invoke_agent), LLM calls (call_llm), tool calls (execute_tool), and data sending (send_data). The tracer is initialized as: `export const tracer = trace.getTracer('gcp.vertex.agent', version);`. Attribute naming follows OpenTelemetry semantic conventions with prefixes: 'gen_ai.*' for standard GenAI attributes (gen_ai.agent.name, gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.system, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, gen_ai.response.finish_reasons) and 'gcp.vertex.agent.*' for GCP-specific attributes (gcp.vertex.agent.llm_request, gcp.vertex.agent.llm_response, gcp.vertex.agent.event_id, gcp.vertex.agent.session_id, gcp.vertex.agent.invocation_id).

const span = tracer.startSpan(`invoke_agent ${this.name}`);
const span = tracer.startSpan('call_llm');
return tracer.startActiveSpan(`execute_tool ${tool.name}`, async (span) => {

answers.answer: OpenTelemetry span attributes recorded for agent invocations include: (1) gen_ai.operation.name: set to 'invoke_agent' (required), (2) gen_ai.agent.name: the agent's name (conditionally required), (3) gen_ai.agent.description: the agent's description (conditionally required), (4) gen_ai.conversation.id: set to invocationContext.session.id (conditionally required). The implementation notes that gen_ai.agent.id is not set due to unclear requirements about uniqueness scope and deployment persistence. The gen_ai.data_source.id is also not set as it's not available. Server attributes are pending confirmation.

OpenTelemetry attributes recorded for LLM calls include: (1) gen_ai.system: set to 'gcp.vertex.agent', (2) gen_ai.request.model: the model name from llmRequest.model, (3) gen_ai.request.top_p: from llmRequest.config?.topP (if present), (4) gen_ai.request.max_tokens: from llmRequest.config?.maxOutputTokens (if present), (5) gen_ai.usage.input_tokens: from llmResponse.usageMetadata.promptTokenCount || 0, (6) gen_ai.usage.output_tokens: from llmResponse.usageMetadata.candidatesTokenCount (if present), (7) gen_ai.response.finish_reasons: array with lowercased finishReason string (if present). Additionally, GCP-specific attributes are recorded: gcp.vertex.agent.invocation_id, gcp.vertex.agent.session_id, gcp.vertex.agent.event_id, gcp.vertex.agent.llm_request (JSON serialized request, controlled by shouldAddRequestResponseToSpans), and gcp.vertex.agent.llm_response (JSON serialized response, controlled by shouldAddRequestResponseToSpans).

The ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS environment variable controls whether request/response content is included in traces via the shouldAddRequestResponseToSpans() function. When set to 'false' or '0', request/response content is replaced with empty JSON objects '{}' in span attributes. When set to 'true' or '1' (or any other value, as 'true' is the default), the full content is serialized and included. The function defaults to true for backward compatibility. This affects attributes like gcp.vertex.agent.llm_request, gcp.vertex.agent.llm_response, gcp.vertex.agent.tool_call_args, gcp.vertex.agent.tool_response, and gcp.vertex.agent.data. The implementation notes that once prompt and response logging is well established, the default might be switched to false to start deprecation of request/response content in spans.
code_snippets:
'gcp.vertex.agent.llm_request': shouldAddRequestResponseToSpans()
  ? safeJsonSerialize(buildLlmRequestForTrace(llmRequest))
  : '{}',

'gcp.vertex.agent.tool_call_args': shouldAddRequestResponseToSpans()
  ? safeJsonSerialize(args)
  : '{}',

'gcp.vertex.agent.tool_response': shouldAddRequestResponseToSpans()
  ? safeJsonSerialize(toolResponse)
  : '{}'

answers.answer: The Google Cloud telemetry integration works via the getGcpExporters function which returns span processors, metric readers, and log record processors based on the OtelExportersConfig. It uses @google-cloud/opentelemetry-cloud-trace-exporter's TraceExporter and @google-cloud/opentelemetry-cloud-monitoring-exporter's MetricExporter. The function first determines the GCP project ID using GoogleAuth from google-auth-library. If enableTracing is true, it creates a BatchSpanProcessor with TraceExporter. If enableMetrics is true, it creates a PeriodicExportingMetricReader with MetricExporter and a 5000ms export interval. For logging, it returns an empty array (currently not implemented). GCP resource detection is performed via getGcpResource() which uses the gcpDetector from @opentelemetry/resource-detector-gcp to populate resource labels. If the project ID cannot be determined, it logs a warning and returns empty hooks.

The runAsyncGeneratorWithOtelContext helper binds OpenTelemetry context to async generators, ensuring trace propagation across yielded values. It takes an otelContext (OpenTelemetry Context), generatorFnContext (the 'this' context), and generatorFn (the generator function to execute). It works by: (1) calling the generator function with the provided 'this' context, (2) binding the OTel context to the resulting generator using bindOtelContextToAsyncGenerator, which wraps the generator's next(), return(), and throw() methods using context.bind() from OpenTelemetry API. This ensures that each method call executes within the provided OpenTelemetry context, maintaining trace continuity across async iterations. The [Symbol.asyncIterator] is also bound to return a context-bound generator.

answers.answer: The OtelExportersConfig and OTelHooks system in setup.ts allows custom span processors and metric readers to be added. OtelExportersConfig has boolean flags: enableTracing, enableMetrics, and enableLogging. OTelHooks interface defines three optional arrays: spanProcessors (SpanProcessor[]), metricReaders (MetricReader[]), and logRecordProcessors (LogRecordProcessor[]). The maybeSetOtelProviders function accepts an array of OTelHooks and an optional OTel resource. It merges all hooks (including OTLP exporters from environment variables) and sets up providers only if the respective arrays are non-empty. For tracing, it creates a NodeTracerProvider with the merged spanProcessors and registers it globally. For metrics, it creates a MeterProvider with merged metricReaders. For logging, it creates a LoggerProvider with merged logRecordProcessors. The function also supports automatic OTLP exporter configuration via environment variables (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT).

The CLI commands available in @google/adk-devtools are: (1) 'web' - Starts the ADK web server with Angular debug UI (serveDebugUI: true), (2) 'api_server' - Starts the ADK API server without debug UI (serveDebugUI: false), (3) 'create' - Scaffolds a new agent project with interactive prompts for model, API key, project, region, and language selection, (4) 'run' - Runs an agent in CLI mode with support for session save/resume and replay from JSON files, (5) 'deploy cloud_run' - Deploys an agent to Google Cloud Run with configuration options for project, region, service name, and UI inclusion. All commands are defined using Commander.js with the Command class.
code_snippets:
program
  .command('create')
  .description('Creates a new agent')
  .argument('[agent]', 'Name to give the new agent', 'adk_agent')

program
  .command('run')
  .description('Runs agent')
  .argument('<agent>', 'Agent file path (.js or .ts)')

DEPLOY_COMMAND.command('cloud_run')
  .addArgument(AGENT_DIR_ARGUMENT)
  .addOption(PORT_OPTION)

answers.answer: The 'adk web' command starts the dev server with Angular debug UI using AdkWebServer with serveDebugUI: true. Options include: --host (-h): binding host (default: os.hostname()), --port (-p): server port (default: '8000'), --allow_origins: CORS allowed origins (default: ''), --verbose (-v): verbose logging (default: false), --log_level: log level (default: 'info', choices: 'debug', 'info', 'warn', 'error'), --session_service_uri: URI for session service (supported: 'memory://' for in-memory, DATABASE_URL env var as fallback), --artifact_service_uri: URI for artifact service (supported: 'gs://<bucket>' for GCS, 'memory://' for in-memory), --otel_to_cloud: send OTel traces to cloud (default: false), --compile: compile TypeScript agent files to JavaScript (default: true), --bundle: bundle agent files (default: true), --file_type: module type (choices: 'cjs', 'esm'). The command accepts an optional [agents_dir] argument defaulting to process.cwd().
code_snippets:
program
  .command('web')
  .description('Start ADK web server')
  .addArgument(AGENT_DIR_ARGUMENT)
  .addOption(HOST_OPTION)
  .addOption(PORT_OPTION)
  .addOption(ORIGINS_OPTION)
  .addOption(VERBOSE_OPTION)
  .addOption(LOG_LEVEL_OPTION)
  .addOption(SESSION_SERVICE_URI_OPTION)
  .addOption(ARTIFACT_SERVICE_URI_OPTION)
  .addOption(OTEL_TO_CLOUD_OPTION)
  .addOption(COMPILE_AGENT_FILE)
  .addOption(BUNDLE_AGENT_FILE)
  .addOption(AGENT_FILE_MODULE_TYPE)

answers.answer: The 'adk create' command scaffolds a new agent project using interactive prompts via the @clack/prompts library. It accepts an optional [agent] argument for the agent name (default: 'adk_agent'). Options include: -y, --yes (skip confirmation prompts), --model (the model for root_agent), --api_key (Google AI API Key), --project (Google Cloud Project for VertexAI), --region (Google Cloud Region for VertexAI), --language (output language: 'ts' or 'js'). The interactive flow prompts for: (1) model selection (gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-3-pro-preview), (2) language choice (TypeScript or JavaScript), (3) backend selection (Google AI or Vertex AI), (4) based on backend: either API key for Google AI, or project ID and region for Vertex AI (with defaults from gcloud config or env vars). It generates files including agent.[ts|js], .env, package.json, and optionally tsconfig.json. The .env file is populated with GOOGLE_API_KEY or GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT/GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION and GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI flag. Finally, it runs npm install for dependencies.
code_snippets:
program
  .command('create')
  .description('Creates a new agent')
  .argument('[agent]', 'Name to give the new agent', 'adk_agent')
  .option('-y, --yes', 'Optional. Skip confirmation prompts.')
  .option('--model <string>', 'Optional. THe model used for the root_agent')
  .option('--api_key <string>', 'Optional. The API Key needed to access the model')
  .option('--project <string>', 'Optional. The Google Cloud Project for using VertexAI as backend.')
  .option('--region <string>', 'Optional. The Google Cloud Region for using VertexAI as backend.')
  .option('--language <string>', 'Optional. Either ts or js as the language to output.')

answers.answer: The 'adk run' command provides CLI-based agent interaction. It requires an <agent> argument specifying the agent file path (.js or .ts). Session management options include: --save_session [boolean] (default: false) to save the session to a JSON file on exit, --session_id <string> to specify the session ID for saving (user is prompted if not set), --resume <string> to load a previously saved session JSON file and continue interaction, --replay <string> to load a JSON file with initial state and user queries, creating a new session and running queries non-interactively. The replay file structure is {state: Record<string, unknown>, queries: string[]}. Additional options include --verbose, --log_level, --session_service_uri, --artifact_service_uri, --otel_to_cloud, --compile, --bundle, and --file_type. The command creates a Runner with InMemorySessionService, InMemoryArtifactService, and InMemoryMemoryService by default. Interactive mode reads user input via readline until 'exit' is entered.
code_snippets:
program
  .command('run')
  .description('Runs agent')
  .argument('<agent>', 'Agent file path (.js or .ts)')
  .option('--save_session [boolean]', 'Optional. Whether to save the session to a json file on exit.', false)
  .option('--session_id <string>', 'Optional. The session ID to save the session to on exit when --save_session is set to true.')
  .option('--replay <string>', 'The json file that contains the initial state of the session and user queries.')
  .option('--resume <string>', 'The json file that contains a previously saved session (by --save_session option).')

answers.answer: The 'adk deploy cloud_run' command deploys agents to Google Cloud Run. Configuration options include: --project (Google Cloud project, defaults to gcloud config value), --region (Google Cloud region, defaults to gcloud config run/region value), --service_name (default: 'adk-default-service-name'), --temp_folder (temp folder for generated files, default: timestamped folder in system temp via getTempDir('cloud_run_deploy_src')), --port (server port, default: '8000'), --adk_version (ADK version to use, default: 'latest'), --with_ui [boolean] (deploy with Web UI, default: false - deploys API server only), --allow_origins (CORS origins), --session_service_uri, --artifact_service_uri, --compile, --bundle, --file_type. The command generates a Dockerfile with node:lts-alpine base, creates a non-root 'myuser', sets environment variables (GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=1, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION), copies agent files and dependencies, and runs 'npx adk web' or 'npx adk api_server' based on with_ui flag. It supports additional gcloud arguments that don't conflict with ADK-managed args (--source, --project, --port, --verbosity, --region). The deployment adds 'created-by=adk' label automatically.
code_snippets:
DEPLOY_COMMAND.command('cloud_run')
  .addArgument(AGENT_DIR_ARGUMENT)
  .addOption(PORT_OPTION)
  .option('--project [string]', 'Optional. Google Cloud project to deploy the agent.')
  .option('--region [string]', 'Optional. Google Cloud region to deploy the agent.')
  .option('--service_name [string]', 'Optional. The service name to use in Cloud Run.', 'adk-default-service-name')
  .option('--temp_folder [string]', 'Optional. Temp folder for the generated Cloud Run source files', getTempDir('cloud_run_deploy_src'))
  .option('--adk_version [string]', 'Optional. ADK version to use in the Cloud Run service.', 'latest')
  .option('--with_ui [boolean]', 'Optional. Deploy ADK Web UI if set. (default: deploy ADK API server only)', false)

answers.answer: The AgentLoader discovers and loads agents from directories with support for both single-file agents and directory-based agents. It accepts agentsDirPath (default: process.cwd()) and AgentFileOptions (compile, bundle, moduleType) in the constructor. The directory structure supports: agents_dir/{agentName}.[js|ts|mjs|cjs] or agents_dir/{agentName}/agent.[js|ts|mjs|cjs]. The listAgents() method returns sorted agent names, and getAgentFile(agentName) returns an AgentFile instance. The compile option (default: true) compiles TypeScript files to JavaScript using esbuild with target: 'node16', platform: 'node', and format determined by module type. The bundle option (default: true) bundles dependencies using esbuild with packages: 'bundle' and minify: true. AgentFileOptions includes compile (boolean), bundle (boolean), and moduleType (FileModuleType.CJS or FileModuleType.ESM). Module type detection follows: .cjs/.cts -> CJS, .mjs/.mts -> ESM, .js/.ts -> determined from nearest package.json 'type' field (module -> ESM, commonjs or missing -> CJS). The AgentFile class uses esbuild with shimPlugin() for compilation.

The agent file loading system supports both ESM and CJS modules via the FileModuleType enum with values 'esm' and 'cjs'. The compile/bundle pipeline uses esbuild to transform TypeScript agent files. When compile or bundle options are true, the AgentFile.load() method: (1) determines the module type from options.moduleType or via getFileModuleType() which examines file extensions (.cjs/.cts -> CJS, .mjs/.mts -> ESM) or package.json 'type' field for .js/.ts files, (2) generates output filename with appropriate extension (.cjs for CJS, .mjs for ESM) via FILE_MODULE_TYPE_EXTENSION_MAP, (3) invokes esbuild.build() with configuration: entryPoints: [filePath], target: 'node16', platform: 'node', format: moduleType (either 'cjs' or 'esm'), packages: 'bundle', bundle: this.options.bundle, minify: this.options.bundle, allowOverwrite: true, plugins: [shimPlugin()]. The compiled file is written to a temp directory (getTempDir('adk_agent_loader')) and imported using dynamic import with pathToFileURL. The AgentFile class manages cleanup via Symbol.asyncDispose and deletes the compiled file on disposal.
code_snippets: const jsModule = await import(pathToFileURL(filePath).href);

answers.answer: The 'adk api_server' command differs from 'adk web' by setting serveDebugUI: false when constructing the AdkWebServer, which means it starts the server without serving the Angular debug UI. Both commands share the same options (host, port, allow_origins, verbose, log_level, session_service_uri, artifact_service_uri, otel_to_cloud, compile, bundle, file_type) and use identical logic except for the serveDebugUI flag. When serveDebugUI is false, the server does not set up the '/' redirect to '/dev-ui' and does not serve the static files from the '../browser' directory. This makes api_server suitable for production deployments where only the REST API endpoints are needed without the development UI overhead.

The REST API endpoints provided by AdkWebServer for session management are: (1) GET /apps/:appName/users/:userId/sessions/:sessionId - retrieves a specific session by ID, returns 404 if not found, (2) GET /apps/:appName/users/:userId/sessions - lists all sessions for a user, (3) POST /apps/:appName/users/:userId/sessions/:sessionId - creates a new session with specified ID, accepts {state: Record<string, unknown>} in body, returns 400 if session already exists, (4) POST /apps/:appName/users/:userId/sessions - creates a new session with auto-generated ID, accepts {state: Record<string, unknown>} in body, (5) DELETE /apps/:appName/users/:userId/sessions/:sessionId - deletes a session, returns 404 if not found, returns 204 on success. All endpoints use the sessionService (BaseSessionService) for operations and return JSON responses with appropriate error handling (500 status for exceptions).

The REST API endpoints for artifact management are: (1) GET /apps/:appName/users/:userId/sessions/:sessionId/artifacts/:artifactName - loads the latest version of an artifact, returns 404 if not found, (2) GET /apps/:appName/users/:userId/sessions/:sessionId/artifacts/:artifactName/versions/:versionId - loads a specific version of an artifact by parsing versionId to integer, returns 404 if not found, (3) GET /apps/:appName/users/:userId/sessions/:sessionId/artifacts - lists all artifact keys (filenames) for a session, (4) GET /apps/:appName/users/:userId/sessions/:sessionId/artifacts/:artifactName/versions - lists all version numbers for a specific artifact, (5) DELETE /apps/:appName/users/:userId/sessions/:sessionId/artifacts/:artifactName - deletes an artifact and all its versions, returns 204 on success. All endpoints use the artifactService (BaseArtifactService) and call methods: loadArtifact({appName, userId, sessionId, filename, version?}), listArtifactKeys({appName, userId, sessionId}), listVersions({appName, userId, sessionId, filename}), deleteArtifact({appName, userId, sessionId, filename}).

The POST /run endpoint accepts a request body with fields: appName (string, identifies the agent), userId (string, identifies the user), sessionId (string, identifies the session), newMessage (Content object with role and parts), and stateDelta (optional, Record<string, unknown> for state updates). The endpoint: (1) validates the session exists (returns 404 if not found), (2) loads the agent using agentLoader.getAgentFile(appName), (3) gets or creates a Runner for the app, (4) collects all events from runner.runAsync({userId, sessionId, newMessage, stateDelta}), (5) returns an array of Event objects as JSON response. If any error occurs, it returns 500 status with {error: message}. The response is a complete array of events accumulated from the async generator, not streamed.

The debug endpoints available are: (1) GET /debug/trace/:eventId - retrieves trace data for a specific event ID from the traceDict, returns the event's span attributes including trace_id, span_id, gen_ai.*, gcp.vertex.agent.* attributes, returns 404 if trace not found, (2) GET /debug/trace/session/:sessionId - retrieves all trace spans for a session from the memoryExporter, returns an array of span data objects with fields: name (span name), span_id, trace_id, start_time (nanoseconds via hrTimeToNanoseconds), end_time (nanoseconds), attributes (all span attributes), parent_span_id (or null), returns empty array if no traces found. The traceDict is populated by ApiServerSpanExporter which filters spans with names 'call_llm', 'send_data', or starting with 'execute_tool' and stores them by gcp.vertex.agent.event_id. The memoryExporter (InMemoryExporter) tracks spans by session ID, indexing them by trace IDs extracted from 'call_llm' spans.

The GET /list-apps endpoint discovers available agents via the AgentLoader by calling agentLoader.listAgents(), which returns a sorted array of agent names. If successful, it responds with JSON array of agent names. If an error occurs (e.g., agent loading failure), it returns 500 status with {error: message}. The AgentLoader scans the agentsDir for agent files following the structure: agents_dir/{agentName}.[js|ts|mjs|cjs] or agents_dir/{agentName}/agent.[js|ts|mjs|cjs], preloads them to verify they export a valid BaseAgent instance, and returns the names as sorted keys from the preloadedAgents dictionary.

The agent graph visualization endpoint GET /apps/:appName/users/:userId/sessions/:sessionId/events/:eventId/graph works by: (1) retrieving the session via sessionService.getSession(), returning 404 if not found, (2) finding the event by eventId in session.events, returning 404 if not found, (3) loading the root agent via agentLoader.getAgentFile(appName), (4) extracting function calls and function responses from the event using getFunctionCalls() and getFunctionResponses(), (5) building highlight tuples: for function calls, pairs are [event.author, functionCall.name]; for function responses, pairs are [functionResponse.name, event.author], (6) calling getAgentGraphAsDot(rootAgent, functionCallHighlights) which returns DOT format graph source, (7) responding with JSON: {dotSrc: string}. If the event has no function calls or responses, it creates a highlight with [event.author, ''] to show the active agent. The DOT format can be rendered by graph visualization tools.

The planned but not-yet-implemented eval set endpoints and their intended purposes are: (1) POST /apps/:appName/eval_sets/:evalSetId - create a new evaluation set, (2) GET /apps/:appName/eval_sets - list all evaluation sets for an app, (3) POST /apps/:appName/eval_sets/:evalSetId/add_session - add a session to an evaluation set, (4) GET /apps/:appName/eval_sets/:evalSetId/evals - get all evaluation cases in an eval set, (5) GET /apps/:appName/eval_sets/:evalSetId/evals/:evalCaseId - get a specific evaluation case, (6) PUT /apps/:appName/eval_sets/:evalSetId/evals/:evalCaseId - update an evaluation case, (7) DELETE /apps/:appName/eval_sets/:evalSetId/evals/:evalCaseId - delete an evaluation case, (8) POST /apps/:appName/eval_sets/:evalSetId/run_eval - run evaluation on an eval set. Additionally, eval results endpoints: (9) GET /apps/:appName/eval_results/:evalResultId - get specific eval result, (10) GET /apps/:appName/eval_results - list all eval results, (11) GET /apps/:appName/eval_metrics - get evaluation metrics. All these endpoints currently return 501 status with {error: 'Not implemented'}. The intended purpose is to support systematic agent evaluation and testing workflows.

The AdkWebServer handles CORS configuration via the allowOrigins option. If allowOrigins is provided, the server configures CORS middleware using the cors package with {origin: allowOrigins}. The express middleware stack is set up in order: (1) CORS middleware (if allowOrigins is set), (2) express.urlencoded({limit: '50mb', extended: true}) for parsing URL-encoded request bodies, (3) express.json({limit: '50mb'}) for parsing JSON request bodies. Both body parsers have a 50MB limit to handle large payloads including artifacts and file uploads. If serveDebugUI is true, static file serving middleware is also added for the /dev-ui route using express.static() with custom headers to set Content-Type for .js files.

The runner caching mechanism in AdkWebServer works via the runnerCache private property, which is a Record<string, Runner> dictionary mapping appName to Runner instances. The getRunner(agent: BaseAgent, appName: string) method implements the cache logic: (1) checks if appName exists as a key in runnerCache, (2) if not found, creates a new Runner with configuration {appName, agent, memoryService, sessionService, artifactService} and stores it in runnerCache[appName], (3) returns the cached (or newly created) Runner instance. This avoids recreating Runner instances on every request to the same agent, which would be expensive as Runner initialization involves setting up services and plugin infrastructure. The cache persists for the lifetime of the AdkWebServer instance.
code_snippets: private readonly runnerCache: Record<string, Runner> = {};

answers.answer: The ServerOptions interface for configuring AdkWebServer includes: agentsDir (string, optional): directory containing agent files, host (string, optional): binding host (default: 'localhost'), port (number, optional): server port (default: 8000), sessionService (BaseSessionService, optional): custom session service implementation (default: InMemorySessionService), memoryService (BaseMemoryService, optional): custom memory service implementation (default: InMemoryMemoryService), artifactService (BaseArtifactService, optional): custom artifact service implementation (default: InMemoryArtifactService), agentLoader (AgentLoader, optional): custom agent loader (default: new AgentLoader with agentsDir and agentFileLoadOptions), agentFileLoadOptions (AgentFileOptions, optional): options for loading agent files (compile, bundle, moduleType), serveDebugUI (boolean, optional): whether to serve the Angular debug UI (default: false), allowOrigins (string, optional): CORS allowed origins, otelToCloud (boolean, optional): send OTel traces to cloud (default: false), registerProcessors ((tracerProvider: TracerProvider) => void, optional): callback to register custom span processors with the tracer provider.

The AdkWebServer sets up telemetry in the setupTelemetry() private async method with internal span exporters and optional Google Cloud trace export. It creates two internal exporters: (1) ApiServerSpanExporter(this.traceDict) - filters and stores spans with names 'call_llm', 'send_data', or starting with 'execute_tool' by event ID for the /debug/trace/:eventId endpoint, (2) InMemoryExporter(this.sessionTraceDict) - tracks 'call_llm' spans by session ID for the /debug/trace/session/:sessionId endpoint. Both are wrapped in SimpleSpanProcessor instances. The method calls setupTelemetry(this.otelToCloud, internalExporters) from telemetry_utils, which: if otelToCloud is true, calls setupGcpTelemetryExperimental() to add GCP trace and metric exporters via getGcpExporters({enableTracing: true, enableLogging: false, enableMetrics: true}) and getGcpResource(); otherwise, if OTEL environment variables are set (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, etc.), it calls setupTelemetryFromEnvExperimental(); else it just sets up the internal exporters. Finally, if registerProcessors callback is provided in ServerOptions, it's called with the global tracer provider to allow custom span processor registration.
